source: Lab learning story (Rachel), PR-TFX primer iterations 002/003/004 (Feb-Mar 2026)
note: Categorical compatibility boundaries (material A + material B -> catastrophic failure), distinct from continuous threshold boundaries (deriveBoundary). Captured as a real learning event: where the system BREAKS.

trigger.to: PR-TFX primer (zinc borate + zinc phosphate + melamine-bearing emulsions 2403/58)

boundaries.failure: rapid gelation / 'shock' on addition -> cracked, non-uniform film, poor/no cure

evidence.isolation_tests: K-silicate added to small primer aliquots hardened EVERY time, across TYPES (KSIL34, P35, KASIL 2135, K28) and DILUTIONS (20/35/50% water).

iterations.result_24h: did not cure; many cracks, slight adhesion

iterations.result_10d: 2 coats ~130um, fewer cracks than 002 but non-uniform, cracks

iterations.approach: replaced K-silicate with extra 2403 emulsion + water; added zinc dust
iterations.result_4d: 2 coats, smooth film with MICRO-cracks, ~55um avg

boundaries.verified_claim: Adding ANY potassium silicate (type/dilution-independent) to this PR-TFX primer causes shock/gelation -> film failure. Robust across repeated controlled mini-tests.
boundaries.open_attribution: WHICH component reacts with K-silicate is NOT isolated. Candidates: zinc_borate, zinc_phosphate, melamine, emulsion_2403, emulsion_58.
boundaries.to_verify: One-component-at-a-time isolation: K-silicate + ONLY zinc_borate; + ONLY zinc_phosphate; + ONLY melamine; + ONLY each emulsion. The one(s) that gel = the culprit; the rest = the bypass route (R&D payoff).
boundaries.trend: 002 (no cure, many cracks) -> 003 (130um, fewer) -> 004 (55um, smooth, micro-cracks). Managing/removing K-silicate improves film; micro-cracks persist.
